selection.rationale: Objective is generated_tokens_per_second = 256 tokens over the end-to-end wall of the frozen workload (batch 8, 256 prompt tokens, 32 fixed-length greedy tokens; full workload always executes; single device, communication not applicable). Clean original baseline: 831.2 ms wall = 124.8 ms prefill + 706.4 ms decode, 308.0 tok/s; 85% of the wall is the 31-step decode loop inside the editable call boundary (provider config and opop_adapter/opop_evaluate are fixed). Hooked diagnostics are used only as bounds, never as wall claims: the decode phase runs about 2,073 kernel launches per step (about 7 us mean) with 447.5 ms GPU busy against the 706.4 ms clean decode wall, i.e. roughly 259 ms (about 8.4 ms per step, about 37% of decode) is host dispatch and launch-gap overhead, while prefill is already GPU-busy-bound (131.2 ms busy vs 124.8 ms wall) and offers no comparable idle headroom. This host-dispatch removal is the only large editable lever: the dominant busy time is GEMM kernels whose operator/provider selection is not an editable boundary here, GEMMs already run near the weight-bandwidth floor, and speculative or draft decoding is excluded by the exact single-model greedy invariants. Repair of the concrete failure of trial-eeb66b190e (inputs/previous-feedback.txt), which selected this same region and mechanism class and was rejected as no_valid_parameter_candidate after both paired quality repeats failed identically: 26.8% mismatched logits elements, max abs error 4.0 at (0,7,13435), max relative error 111616 at (0,23,91049), with coverage 62/62 engaged, zero fallbacks and math_policy_unchanged=true. That signature does not indicate corrupted computation: garbage or mis-bound KV produces logit deltas of tens of units, whereas 4.0 is exactly the scale of logits differences between different decode positions, and the huge relative error occurs only where the reference logit is near zero. The failed implementation returned the per-step logits as a reused static graph-pool buffer while the frozen adapter quality path appends detached views (output.logits[:, -1].detach(), adapter.py line 168 / source qwen_inference.py line 32) and stacks them only after the final decode step, so every stacked row read the last replay's contents; its conditional clone-when-quality-mode guard could never fire because a call replacement cannot observe the adapter state mode. The per-step argmax, taken before the next replay, stayed exact, which is why only the logits comparison failed, deterministically and identically on both repeats. The repaired candidate keeps the identical measured overhead target and kernel sequence and removes exactly this observation aliasing: the returned per-step logits slice is unconditionally materialized into a fresh contiguous tensor on every invocation (about 2.4 MB, microseconds, paid identically in measure and quality mode so the executed work stays identical), and the compute path is never rewritten. Boundary: region anchored on group c87ceac9604a34476cf4 (Qwen3ForCausalLM decode module call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations, kwargs input_ids [8,1] int64, past_key_values DynamicCache, use_cache True, logits_to_keep 1) covering all 23,261 observed decode-phase calls of the current discovery (decoder layers, Linear/aten::linear, Qwen3MLP, Qwen3Attention, mask-free SDPA, the RMSNorm mean/pow/rsqrt/mul chains, rotary mul/neg/cat, DynamicCache aten::cat appends, dtype casts, and the loop-level argmax), because all of them execute inside the restructured decode step. Earlier lesson from trial-7ee056ddc4 is retained: the only permitted fallback is the pristine parent forward, never an eager static-cache wrapper, which was that trial's KV corruption path. Not selected: prefill (busy-bound, 15% share), GEMM operator replacement (fixed provider, numerics risk against exact greedy tokens), speculative decoding (invariant violation), elementwise numeric fusion (unneeded quality risk while a value-identical mechanism remains).
selection.hypothesis: Whole-step CUDA-graph replay of the unmodified decode forward, repairing the observation aliasing that rejected trial-eeb66b190e. One graph is captured per absolute decode position (31 graphs; geometry deterministic: cache length 256+s, q_len 1) around the pristine parent Qwen3ForCausalLM forward, including its genuine DynamicCache.update torch.cat appends and the observed mask-free SDPA calls (attn_mask=None, is_causal=False at q_len 1); all graphs share one private memory pool and are captured strictly in replay order. Per step the callable copies the greedy token into a static int64 [8,1] buffer, replays that position graph, computes nothing else, and RETURNS output.logits[:, -1] as an unconditionally freshly allocated contiguous clone on every invocation (never a view of pool memory, never mode-dependent) so the adapter quality path that appends detached views and stacks them after the last step can never alias across replays; per-step argmax and tokens are unchanged. Step 0 of every run binds the fresh eager prefill cache into the captured static tensors by pure device copies, torch.equal-verified during development, so each run replays on its own real prefill data. Any guard mismatch (geometry, dtype, cache type, kwargs), capture failure, or replay exception falls back to the pristine parent forward with the original arguments - never to an eager static-cache wrapper, the corruption path of trial-7ee056ddc4 - and capture/warmup happens only inside the untimed warmup runs (request warmup=2). Testable predictions: decode wall falls from 706 ms toward 460-540 ms (GPU busy plus residual copy/replay dispatch), end-to-end from 831 ms to roughly 590-680 ms, raising generated_tokens_per_second from 308.0 to about 377-434 tok/s (+22-41%). Acceptance gates: exact greedy token equality and stacked last-position logits within atol=rtol=0.02 on both paired repeats (the gate trial-eeb66b190e failed), per-step KV slices and per-step returned logits torch.equal to an eager reference during development, no capture cost inside the timed boundary, identical executed work in measure and quality modes. If any gate fails the candidate is rejected; the predicted benefit is a hypothesis to be tested, not a guaranteed gain.

proposal.rationale: Repair of trial-eeb66b190e (inputs/previous-feedback.txt), which selected this same region (group c87ceac9604a34476cf4) and mechanism class and was rejected after both paired quality repeats failed identically: 26.8% mismatched logits elements, max abs error 4.0 at (0,7,13435), max relative error 111616 at (0,23,91049), coverage 62/62 engaged with zero fallbacks and math_policy_unchanged=true. That signature is observation aliasing, not corrupted computation: 4.0 is exactly the scale of logits differences between decode positions, the huge relative errors sit where the reference logit is near zero, the per-step argmax (taken before the next replay) stayed exact, and the failure was deterministic on both repeats. The failed implementation returned the per-step logits as a reused static graph-pool buffer while the frozen adapter quality path appends detached views (output.logits[:, -1].detach(), adapter.py lines 152/168) and stacks them only after the last decode step, so every stacked row read the final replay's contents; its conditional clone-when-quality-mode guard could never fire because a call replacement must not branch on adapter mode. This attempt changes exactly that: the replacement returns output.logits[:, -1] as an unconditionally freshly allocated contiguous clone (about 2.4 MB, microseconds) on every invocation - never a view of pool memory, never mode-dependent - so measure and quality modes execute identical work and the stacked comparison sees each step's own values. Everything else keeps the mechanically proven policy of that trial: one CUDA graph per absolute decode position (31 graphs; geometry deterministic: cache length 256+s, q_len 1) captured strictly in replay order around the pristine parent Qwen3ForCausalLM forward, including its genuine DynamicCache.update torch.cat appends (transformers 5.16.1 DynamicLayer/DynamicCache verified in the installed source) and the mask-free SDPA calls (attn_mask=None, is_causal=False at q_len 1); all graphs share one torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle private pool; per step the callable copies the greedy token into a static int64 [8,1] buffer, replays that position graph (one replay instead of about 2,073 kernel launches per step observed in target-resources.json) and returns the fresh clone plus the marker DynamicCache - an exact DynamicCache instance, so the framework signature guard accepts it at every step and the candidate stays engaged (the 62/62 coverage of the failed trial proves this path). Step 0 of every run binds the fresh eager prefill cache into the static buffers by pure device copies (72 tensors [8,8,256,128] bf16, about 288 MiB), so each run replays on its own real prefill data and nothing fixture-dependent is cached; prefill itself stays eager and untouched. New runs are detected by cache-object identity (incoming cache is not the marker), and the observed marker geometry is re-checked per step (length 256+step, 36 layers). Any guard mismatch (positional args, extra/missing kwargs, use_cache/logits_to_keep values, input_ids shape/dtype, cache type or geometry), any capture failure or any replay exception latches to the pristine parent forward with the original arguments - never to an eager static-cache wrapper, which was trial-7ee056ddc4's KV corruption path - and a mid-run fallback first restores the last known-good marker tensors and clones them so no graph-owned state is mutated by the eager parent. Baseline bounds (hooked diagnostics, never wall claims): decode 447.5 ms GPU busy inside a 706.4 ms decode wall of the 831.2 ms end-to-end workload, about 8.4 ms/step host dispatch and launch-gap overhead (37% of decode) while prefill is busy-bound (131.2 ms busy vs 124.8 ms wall). Testable prediction: decode wall falls toward 460-540 ms, end-to-end toward 590-680 ms, raising generated_tokens_per_second from 308.0 to roughly 377-434 tok/s over the frozen batch 8 x 256-prompt x 32-greedy-token workload; the predicted benefit is a hypothesis to be tested, not a guaranteed gain. Single device, so no communication component exists.

setup_work.build_time: build(context) performs no allocation and no GPU work; it binds the parent forward from context['references'], the module from context['modules'], reads frozen geometry from state (prompt_tokens=256, new_tokens=32 -> 31 decode steps) and the layer count from the model config, and returns the single-call mapping {323bcbe006b343648b346af9: replacement}.
setup_work.static_buffers: allocated once, lazily, on the first decode step of the first run that reaches the decode loop (request warmup=2 precedes measurement, so this is untimed): 36 layers x key/value torch.empty_like([8,8,256,128] bfloat16) = 72 tensors, about 288 MiB, plus one static [8,1] int64 token buffer and one marker DynamicCache(config=model.config) whose 36 DynamicLayers are bound to the static tensors; retained for the process lifetime. Model parameters are untouched: no packing, no dtype or layout changes; the graphs reference the existing weight tensors in place.
setup_work.cuda_graphs: 31 per-position torch.cuda.CUDAGraph objects sharing one torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle() private pool, captured strictly in replay order (position 0 first) during the first untimed run; each capture does 2 (position 0) or 1 (later positions) side-stream eager warmup iterations of the pristine parent forward, restores the marker layer references, captures the parent forward reading the static token buffer and the static/previous-pool cache tensors, then replays once and synchronizes. Estimated 2-8 s one-time host cost.
setup_work.retained_graph_pool: all per-step torch.cat outputs are kept alive by explicit references (kv_history plus the marker), so the private pool retains sum over s=0..30 of 72 tensors of length 257+s: about 9.3 GiB, plus 31 static logits buffers [8,1,151936] bfloat16 (about 75 MiB) and per-graph temporaries. This retention prevents any intra-pool block reuse across replays. reserved_bytes grows accordingly and per-run peak_allocated counters include these live allocations: steady state is about 18-19.5 GiB including the 8.05 GiB weights on the 24 GiB device - an accounting and reservation increase, not a memory saving.
setup_work.per_run_work: inside the timed boundary: at step 0, 72 device copies of the run's real eager prefill K/V into the static buffers (about 288 MiB, about 0.5 ms); per decode step, one [8,1] int64 copy_ into the static token buffer, one graph replay, and one unconditionally fresh [8,1,151936] bfloat16 logits clone (about 2.4 MiB) - identical executed work in measure and quality modes; the adapter's per-step argmax, token bookkeeping and final torch.cat are unchanged and stay eager. Capture and warmup never occur inside timed repeats; a fresh run is detected by cache identity and re-binds its own prefill data, so the full workload executes on every invocation and no fixture-dependent output is cached.

quality_risks: Hard gates are exact greedy tokens and logits within atol=rtol=0.02 on both paired repeats (the gate trial-eeb66b190e failed). Replay re-executes the same deterministic kernels the eager parent would run (allow_tf32 False, cudnn.benchmark False, fixed shapes per position, eval mode without dropout), with per-run input data bound by device copies from that run's own eager prefill, so token equality and tolerance are expected; any kernel dispatch difference between eager and captured execution would surface as a quality failure and the candidate is rejected.

The repaired defect: the returned logits slice is a fresh contiguous clone on every invocation, never a view of the static graph-pool buffer and never conditional on adapter mode, so the adapter's append-then-stack quality path cannot alias across replays; the per-step argmax still consumes the same values it would have consumed eagerly.

The KV data path is intentionally not rewritten: the captured forward is the unmodified parent with real DynamicCache concatenation (direct repair of trial-7ee056ddc4's static-cache corruption), and the returned past_key_values is an exact DynamicCache instance so the framework signature guard keeps the candidate engaged at all 31 steps per run instead of falling back mid-run.

Any capture failure (uncapturable op, pool error) or replay exception disables the graph path permanently for the process and every call degrades to the pristine parent forward with the original arguments; a mid-run fallback restores the last known-good marker tensor references and passes a clone, so no graph-owned tensor is mutated by the eager parent - no speedup, quality preserved.

The first run reaching the decode loop pays warmup plus capture for all 31 positions inside its (untimed) wall; request warmup=2 and the quality runs precede measurement, so no timed sample pays capture cost. If capture ever occurred inside a timed run, that sample would be slow, not wrong.

Geometry is frozen (batch 8, prompt 256, 31 decode steps, bfloat16, 36 layers); any other signature - positional args, extra kwargs, use_cache/logits_to_keep deviations, input shape or dtype, cache type, layer count or cache length - is guarded to the parent, and a run that somehow extended past 31 decode steps continues eagerly via cloned caches.

Memory: about 9.6 GiB retained statics+graph pool on the 24 GiB device in addition to the 8.05 GiB weights and the baseline eager caches; per-run peak_allocated counters rise accordingly. If allocation failed, the latch falls back to the pristine parent rather than corrupting outputs.
